cards.name: Dragonite V
cards.notes: Dragonite V from Evolving Skies 192/203 is included in this guide as a sleepy Pokemon card for collectors building a calm, cozy, or nap-themed binder. As a Rare Ultra, it is one of the showier entries in the sleepy Pokemon theme and can carry a page on its own. The card is illustrated by Atsushi Furusawa, which is useful context for collectors who like arranging pages by artist as well as by Pokemon. Its high market price puts it firmly in grail territory for a sleepy Pokemon collection, so it is best treated as a long-term chase card. It works nicely in a Sword & Shield-era page, especially alongside Trainer Gallery and alternate-art sleepy cards.
cards.whyItBelongs: Out cold drifting through midair. The undisputed crown jewel of modern sleepy alt-arts and one of the era's definitive grails.

cards.name: Munna
cards.notes: Suggested by the Sleepy Pokemon community. Two Pidove are tucked into the ledge beneath Munna's dreamy pink twilight.
cards.whyItBelongs: Munna floats through a dreamy pink twilight under a crescent moon, radiating sweet dreams with its 'Rest' attack. Down in the foreground, two little Pidoves are cuddled together on the ledge, sound asleep with eyes softly shut. A quiet, poetic Unova bedtime scene.

cards.name: Pikachu
cards.notes: Pikachu from Lost Origin Trainer Gallery TG05/TG30 is included in this guide as a sleepy Pokemon card for collectors building a calm, cozy, or nap-themed binder. As a Trainer Gallery Rare Holo, it connects nicely with the characterful, scene-driven side of modern Pokemon card collecting. The card is illustrated by Atsushi Furusawa, which is useful context for collectors who like arranging pages by artist as well as by Pokemon. Its higher market price makes it feel like a centerpiece candidate rather than a casual binder filler. cards.whyItBelongs: Adventure can wait. Akari has curled up beneath a tree for a well-earned nap with Pikachu tucked into her arms, and somehow Pikachu has managed to wriggle half-free without waking either of them. Atsushi Furusawa turns a quiet break in Hisui into an incredibly sweet little snapshot of how comfortable these two are together.
